Reading the frequencies from the heights of the bars: 1 day corresponds to 1 student, 2 days corresponds to 3 students, 3 days corresponds to 2 students, 4 days corresponds to 6 students, 5 days corresponds to 8 students, 6 days corresponds to 3 students, and 7 days corresponds to 2 students. Reasoning: The problem asks for the mean number of days these students exercised last week, so use a weighted average. The total number of exercise days is 1×1 + 2×3 + 3×2 + 4×6 + 5×8 + 6×3 + 7×2 = 1 + 6 + 6 + 24 + 40 + 18 + 14 = 109. The total number of students is 1 + 3 + 2 + 6 + 8 + 3 + 2 = 25. The mean is 109 ÷ 25 = 4.36. Rounded to the nearest hundredth, it is still 4.36.

method.method_draft: Read the bar graph as a frequency table: 1 day has 1 student, 2 days has 3 students, 3 days has 2 students, 4 days has 6 students, 5 days has 8 students, 6 days has 3 students, and 7 days has 2 students. Use the text to identify that the requested statistic is the mean number of exercise days. Compute the weighted mean by multiplying each day value by its number of students, summing those products, and dividing by the total number of students: (1·1 + 2·3 + 3·2 + 4·6 + 5·8 + 6·3 + 7·2) / (1+3+2+6+8+3+2). Round the result to the nearest hundredth.

method.method_draft: Read the same bar graph frequencies, but compute the mean by deviations from a convenient anchor, such as 5 days. Count the total students from the bar heights: 1+3+2+6+8+3+2 = 25. Then compute the total deviation from 5 days: (1−5)·1 + (2−5)·3 + (3−5)·2 + (4−5)·6 + (5−5)·8 + (6−5)·3 + (7−5)·2 = -16. The average deviation is -16/25 = -0.64, so the mean is 5 - 0.64 = 4.36. Round as requested.
